title: Marked square-zero scheme lifts and their cotangent Ext torsors
statement: Let $S\hookrightarrow S'$ be a first order thickening of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-first-order-thickening], with ideal $\mathcal J$ satisfying $\mathcal J^2=0$, and let $f:X\to S$ be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. A marked lift is a flat scheme $X'\to S'$ and an isomorphism $X'\times_{S'}S\cong X$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; arrows preserve this marking. Put $G=f^*\mathcal J$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. Use the Zariski sheaf standard polynomial cotangent complex $L_{X/S}$ [lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison] and $\operatorname{Ext}^j_X(E,G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D(\mathcal O_X)}(E,G[j])$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. If a marked lift exists, its isomorphism classes are a torsor under $\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(L_{X/S},G)$: after choosing one lift each class is uniquely its translate by one group element. The automorphisms of a marked lift inducing the identity on $X$ are canonically the additive group $\operatorname{Ext}^0_X(L_{X/S},G)$. These identifications commute with restriction to open subschemes of $X$ and with maps on square-zero coefficient modules. If $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ for a field $k$ and $S'=\operatorname{Spec}(k\oplus M)$ for a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space $M$, with $(a,m)(b,n)=(ab,an+bm)$, the trivial lift supplies a canonical origin and gives a canonical identification of marked flat deformation classes with $\operatorname{Ext}^1_X(L_{X/k},\mathcal O_X\otimes_kM)$. It is $k$-linear for the deformation operations induced by linear maps of $M$ and addition of square-zero directions; the trivial lift maps to zero. Here the tensor product is sheafified sectionwise tensor [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. For $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, where $A$ is a localization of a finitely generated $k$-algebra, choose a localized polynomial surjection $P\twoheadrightarrow A$ with kernel $J$. This classification agrees with $\operatorname{Ext}^1_A([J/J^2\to\Omega^1_{P/k}\otimes_PA],A\otimes_kM)$, in degrees $-1,0$, via the affine restriction of the sheaf cotangent complex; it is natural under further localizations. These conclusions impose no properness or dimension hypothesis on $X$.

source.place: Tag 0D14 (lemma-deform), using cotangent.tex Tags 08UW (lemma-compare-cotangent-complex-with-naive-ringed-spaces) and 08UZ (lemma-find-obstruction-ringed-spaces); split origin and functoriality: Tags 0GPZ (lemma-extensions-of-relative-ringed-spaces), 0GQ1 and 0GQ2; affine model: more-morphisms.tex Tag 0D0I (lemma-NL-affine).

proof.text: Identify the underlying spaces of $S$ and $S'$ and put $B=\mathcal O_X$, $R=f^{-1}\mathcal O_S$, $R'=f^{-1}\mathcal O_{S'}$, $K=f^{-1}\mathcal J$, so $R'/K=R$. The ideal $\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent on $S$ (as an $\mathcal O_S$-module it is its own conormal module, because $\mathcal J^2=0$); hence $G=B\otimes_R K=f^*\mathcal J$ is quasi-coherent by module pullback. A marked flat lift gives a ring extension $0\to G\to E\to B\to0$ with an $R'$-algebra structure whose map on $K$ is $k\mapsto1\otimes k$: the flat cartesian conormal comparison identifies its actual ideal with $G$. Conversely realize any such extension as a scheme by the Zariski realization lemma. On affine charts write $R'_0\twoheadrightarrow R_0$, kernel $I$, and $E_0\twoheadrightarrow B_0$, kernel $B_0\otimes_{R_0}I$. The prescribed map on $I$ implies $IE_0=G_0$ and $E_0/IE_0=B_0$. The quotient-tensor identification gives $I\otimes_{R'_0}E_0\cong I\otimes_{R_0}B_0=G_0$, and multiplication is the injection $G_0\hookrightarrow E_0$. The nilpotent-ideal flatness criterion now makes $E_0$ flat over $R'_0$, since $B_0$ is flat over $R_0$. The affine flatness criterion gives flatness globally; the quotient says its special fibre is precisely the marked $X$. The realization lemma identifies all marked isomorphisms. Thus marked lifts are exactly these extensions, with their specified base-ideal map.

source.place: Tag 0D14 (lemma-deform), proof; more-morphisms.tex Tags 05YV and 063Y (lemma-deform), including the converse flatness argument

proof.text: Fix a lift extension $E_0$. If $F$ is an $R$-algebra extension of $B$ by $G$, form $E_0+F$ by taking $E_0\times_BF$ and quotienting its kernel by $\{(g,-g):g\in G\}$. Give it the $R'$-structure $r'\mapsto[\rho_0(r'),\rho_F(\bar r')]$, where $\rho_F$ is the base map $R\to F$. It still sends $k\in K$ to $1\otimes k$, so step 1 realizes it as a flat marked lift. Conversely for a lift $E$ form $E-E_0=(E\times_BE_0)/\{(g,g):g\in G\}$. The map $r'\mapsto[\rho(r'),\rho_0(r')]$ kills $K$ and factors through $R$; its kernel is identified with $G$ by $(g,h)\mapsto g-h$. The cancellation $E_0+(E-E_0)\cong E$ sends a local representative $(a_0,[e,b_0])$ to $e+i(g)$, where $a_0-b_0=i_0(g)$. Replacing $(e,b_0)$ by $(e+i(h),b_0+i_0(h))$ replaces $g$ by $g-h$, leaving this formula unchanged; the outer antidiagonal relation also cancels. The same formula, replacing $e$ by a section of $F$, identifies $(E_0+F)-E_0$ with $F$. These maps are local isomorphisms on both kernel and quotient and therefore are isomorphisms of extensions. For three factors the relation is always that the sum of kernel coordinates is zero. Hence $(E_0+F_1)+F_2=E_0+(F_1+F_2)$, and $E_0+(B\oplus G)=E_0$. The sheaf-algebra classification identifies these Baer classes and their addition with $\operatorname{Ext}^1_B(L_{B/R},G)$. Taking $F=E-E_0$ proves both existence and uniqueness of a translating element. This proves the asserted torsor, independently of any properness or dimension assumption.

source.place: Tag 08UC (lemma-choices-ringed-spaces), translation construction; Tags 0GPZ and 0GQ0, expressed as Baer sum and difference

proof.text: Every $R'$-automorphism of a lift that is the identity on $B$ is also the identity on $G$, since $G$ is generated as a $B$-module by the image of $K$. For such an automorphism $\phi$, $\phi(e)-e$ depends only on $p(e)$ and defines $d:B\to G$. Expanding $\phi(ee')$ and using $G^2=0$ gives $d(bb')=b\,d(b')+b'\,d(b)$; $R'$-linearity makes it vanish on $R$. Conversely $e\mapsto e+i(d(p(e)))$ for an $R$-derivation fixes the base and quotient and has inverse given by $-d$. The cross term is zero, so composition corresponds to addition. The derivation identification in the sheaf-algebra Ext lemma gives exactly $\operatorname{Ext}^0_B(L_{B/R},G)$, with no chosen origin.

Restriction to an open applies every displayed formula sectionwise. For a coefficient map $u:G\to H$, push out the kernels and the base-ideal map: on the displayed kernel coordinates it sends $[g,h]$ to $[u(g),u(h)]$. It therefore commutes with Baer addition and difference, and sends $d$ to $ud$. The sheaf-algebra Ext lemma identifies these operations with the induced Ext maps; its open-restriction compatibility uses the same standard sheaf cotangent complex. For general $H$ this assertion is at the level of square-zero extension problems with base-ideal map $uc$; when both problems arise as flat lifts the scheme identification of step 1 applies. Thus no arbitrary coefficient pushout is falsely asserted to remain a flat lift of the same base.

source.place: Tags 0GQ0, 0GQ1, 0GQ2; all pushout and difference operations use the specified base-ideal map

proof.text: For the split base $k\oplus M$, the projection $k\oplus M\to k$ is split by $k\to k\oplus M$. A lift extension is therefore a sheaf of $k$-algebras with square-zero kernel $G=\mathcal O_X\otimes_kM$. Conversely every such extension has the unique base structure $(a,m)\mapsto a\,1+i(1\otimes m)$; multiplication gives $ab\,1+i(a\otimes n+b\otimes m)$, as required. Step 1 makes it a flat lift. The split extension $B\oplus G$ is the trivial family by the fibre-product affine tensor description, and the base-change flatness lemma guarantees it is flat. The sheaf-algebra class map consequently gives the canonical classification, taking the trivial family to zero. A linear map $M\to N$ induces kernel pushout $B\otimes M\to B\otimes N$; it is the base change of the lift. Indeed base change is flat, so step 1 identifies its kernel with $B\otimes_kN$ and quotient with $B$. The base-change map from the old extension induces $1\otimes u$ on its kernel. The induced map from its kernel pushout is the identity on kernel and quotient, hence is an isomorphism. For addition first take the fibre product of two extensions over $B$ (directions $M\oplus M$), then push out the kernel along addition. The Ext lemma sends these operations to coefficient maps and addition. Scalar multiplication is the coefficient map $m\mapsto am$, giving the stated $k$-linearity.

source.place: Tags 0GPZ, 0GQ0, 0GQ2, specialized to the split thickening; more-morphisms.tex Tag 063Y

proof.text: For $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, use the intrinsic affine cotangent comparison to identify the full sheaf complex with $\widetilde{L_{A/k}}$, and $G$ with $\widetilde{A\otimes_kM}$. The affine quasi-coherent derived equivalence identifies their derived Hom groups with those in $D(A)$. The localized polynomial presentation lemma identifies $C=[J/J^2\to\Omega^1_{P/k}\otimes_PA]$ with $\tau_{\geq-1}L_{A/k}$. In the truncation triangle $Q\to L_{A/k}\to C\to Q[1]$, $Q\in D^{\leq-2}$, hence both $\operatorname{Hom}(Q,G[1])$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(Q[1],G[1])$ vanish by t-structure orthogonality. Exactness of Hom out of the triangle makes $\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(C,G)\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_A(L_{A/k},G)$ bijective. This is the required affine model, without a regular-sequence hypothesis on $J$. Every map used here is the canonical presentation or restriction map. The presentation comparison commutes with maps of localized presentations and the intrinsic comparison with smaller affine charts; the standard cotangent localization comparison handles successive localizations. Thus the Ext description and the deformation class commute with every further localization.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q84-bbe526ac5 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes and every cited statement in full. I compared them against Stacks 0D14, 0GPZ, 0GQ0-0GQ2 and 08U8 (defos.tex), 08UW, 08UZ and 08UR (cotangent.tex), and 05YV and 063Y (more-morphisms.tex). The full L can replace NL because 08UW gives NL = τ_{≥-1}L. The realization node matches 05YV hypothesis by hypothesis, and its morphism clause is true because the kernels are nilpotent and the underlying space is the same. The extension-Ext node is 0GPZ for the identity map of (T,R) to (T,A), with 0GQ0/0GQ2 giving the pushout and Baer-sum compatibility, Der equal to Hom(L,G[0]) since H^0(L)=Ω, and arbitrary G allowed. Neither new node duplicates an existing one: the étale, algebraic-space and ring versions differ, and neither restates a clause of the item. Steps checked: step 1 is the conormal flat base change plus the nilpotent flatness criterion, using the tensor-over-quotient identification and I^2=0. Step 2's Baer sum and difference formulas are invariant under both relations and give existence and uniqueness of the translate. In step 3, G is generated by the image of K, so the automorphism fixes G and d is an R-derivation. Step 4's pushouts work at the level of extension problems. Step 5's unique (k⊕M)-structure is multiplicative because the kernel has square zero, and base change is the kernel pushout. In step 6, Q lies in D^{≤-2}, so Hom(Q,G[1]) and Hom(Q[1],G[1]) both vanish, and the localized presentation is allowed by the naive model. Edge cases G=0, M=0, X empty and non-separated X all hold. Batch-5: lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation (only its affine-chart clause is used), lem-trf-lci-naive-cotangent-model and lem-trf-affine-cotangent-comparison are generic cotangent-complex foundations; their closures (882, 521 and 668 nodes) reach no trace-formula, Lefschetz or Poincaré-duality theorem, so I accept them. All seven split_report.tool_uses are generic and accepted. No SGA source is used and nothing was changed. Maintainer note: the base contains a duplicate pair, lem-sfb-nilpotent-ideal-flatness-criterion and lem-sfb-nilpotent-ideal-module-flatness.
